sections.section_title: 1. Clinical Presentation and Initial Diagnostic Work‑up
sections.description: Outlines the patient’s history, physical findings, laboratory and imaging data that directed the initial differential diagnosis and set the stage for targeted investigations.
subtopics: History of progressive fatigue, weight loss, and dyspnea; onset and progression of symptoms; age and demographic context
Physical examination: pallor, icterus, premature greying, mucosal changes, musculoskeletal findings, hepatosplenomegaly, pulmonary signs

Baseline complete blood count with low reticulocyte count and peripheral smear morphology (dimorphic erythrocytes, basophilic stippling, Cabot rings, hypersegmented neutrophils); interpretation as ineffective erythropoiesis
Serum studies: B12 and folate deficiencies, iron studies (high ferritin and serum iron), inflammatory markers; importance of ruling out other causes of cytopenia
Bone marrow aspirate: trilineage hematopoiesis, erythroid hyperplasia, increased iron stores; cytogenetics; absence of dysplasia or malignancy
Hepatic assessment: ultrasound, transient elastography findings of steatosis and cirrhosis; autoimmune and infectious work‑up; significance of negative serologies
Pulmonary imaging: PET-CT findings of ground‑glass haziness, fibrosis, and subpleural atelectasis; relevance to interstitial lung disease
Additional organ involvement: osteopenia/osteoporosis on DEXA, secondary hyperparathyroidism, electrochemical disturbances, neuropathy (EMG/NCS)

sections.description: Explains the systematic narrowing of causes from common nutritional deficiencies to rarer inherited disorders, emphasizing criteria that shift suspicion toward telomere biology disorders.
subtopics: Initial consideration of vitamin B12/folate deficiency and ineffective erythropoiesis; role of B12 deficiency in anemia, neuropathy, and hypersegmented neutrophils
Evaluation of immune-mediated cytopenia: positive DAT, lack of hemolysis, negative autoimmune panel
Assessment of hepatic fibrosis: exclusion of autoimmune hepatitis, viral hepatitis, alcohol-related disease, and metabolic causes; significance of cirrhosis in a young adult
Pulmonary fibrosis: differential of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) vs. pulmonary infectious or inflammatory causes; relevance of age and lack of environmental exposures
Systemic premature ageing features: greying, nail changes, mucosal atrophy; their classical association with dyskeratosis congenita (DC) and why they were subclinical here
Inclusion of telomere biology disorders (TBDs) in the differential when multisystem involvement is present without typical mucocutaneous triad

Red‑flags prompting genetic testing: persistent cytopenia even after vitamin correction, organ fibrosis, early-onset osteoporosis, neuropathy, and absence of family history (possible de novo mutation)

sections.description: Details the use of exome sequencing, interpretation of the identified variant, and the biological role of PARN in telomere maintenance that explains the observed phenotype.
subtopics: Overview of clinical exome sequencing workflow; germline vs. somatic variants
Identification of monoallelic PARN missense variant c.613T>C (p.Cys205Arg); criteria for Variant of Uncertain Significance (VUS) per ACMG/AMP
Functional importance of the R3H domain and conservation of Cys205; in silico prediction tools and their concordance
Role of PARN in RNA deadenylation and TERC maturation; mechanisms by which PARN haploinsufficiency impairs telomerase activity and telomere elongation

Phenotypic spectrum of PARN mutations: autosomal recessive DC (DKCB6), Hoyeraals–Hreidarsson, telomere‑related pulmonary fibrosis, and bone marrow failure; comparison with other TBD genes (TERT, TERC, RTEL1)
Concept of incomplete penetrance, somatic rescue, and variable expressivity in TBDs; environmental modifiers that influence organ-specific disease onset

sections.description: Describes the therapeutic interventions undertaken, the rationale for supportive care, and the surveillance plan for organ systems potentially affected by telomere attrition.
subtopics: Correction of B12 deficiency: parenteral cyanocobalamin regimen; monitoring response via CBC and reticulocyte index
Supportive hematology: transfusion thresholds, folic acid supplementation, iron homeostasis monitoring, and evaluation for aplastic anemia
Bone health: calcium and vitamin D replacement, bisphosphonate consideration, weight‑bearing exercise; management of secondary hyperparathyroidism
Cardiopulmonary monitoring: pulmonary function tests, high‑resolution CT surveillance, corticosteroid use in IPF, consideration of antifibrotic therapy (e.g., pirfenidone, nintedanib)
Hepatic surveillance: serial elastography, liver function tests, evaluation for portal hypertension; liver transplantation candidacy if decompensation
Future therapeutic avenues: androgen therapy (danazol, nandrolone) for telomere elongation; potential role of hematopoietic stem cell transplantation for marrow failure; data gaps and ongoing trials
Genetic counseling: disclosure of VUS, implications for family planning, cascade testing strategy, reproductive options, and ethical considerations
sections.final_considerations: Educational emphasis on recognizing TBDs as a unifying diagnosis in young adults with unexplained multisystem disease, importance of early genetic testing, and multidisciplinary follow‑up to mitigate progression to organ failure.
